output.summary: KEP-1669 proposes that kube-proxy send traffic to terminating endpoints that are still Ready when all endpoints for a Service (scoped to its traffic policy) are terminating. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale: kube-proxy forwarded traffic only to Ready, non-terminating pods, so rolling updates with externalTrafficPolicy=Local could blackhole traffic while load balancer health checks still routed to the node. Building on KEP-1672's Serving and Terminating EndpointSlice conditions, the KEP falls back to terminating-but-Ready pods only when no other endpoints are available. The source does not say more about why this design was chosen over the listed workarounds beyond noting that kube-proxy handling would remove the need for them.

alternatives.option: Use scheduling/deployment features so a node never has only terminating endpoints
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists this as a workaround users can apply today, not as a Kubernetes-side fix; it constrains deployments rather than handling the complexity in Kubernetes.

alternatives.option: Reduce the load balancer health check interval
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this may not always be possible depending on the load balancer implementation.

alternatives.option: Use a preStop hook to delay SIGTERM
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this may work in some scenarios, but better handling from kube-proxy would alleviate the need for this workaround altogether.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes that if all endpoints for a given Service scoped to its traffic policy are terminating (i.e. pod.DeletionTimestamp != nil), then all traffic should be sent to terminating Pods that are still Ready.

Upon performing a rolling update of a Deployment, there can be a small window of time where old pods on a node are terminating (hence not "Ready") but the load balancer has not probed kube-proxy's healthCheckNodePort yet.
Even though the EndpointSlice API now includes terminating endpoints, kube-proxy strictly forwards traffic to only "Ready" pods that are not terminating.
Reduce potential traffic loss from kube-proxy that occurs on rolling updates because traffic is sent to Pods that are terminating.
